legend: Hypercellular marrow with increased megakaryocytes with atypical features. There is prominent erythroid proliferation in the background. The findings do not meet the criteria for polycythaemia vera, essential thrombocythaemia, or primary myelofibrosis. Next-generation sequencing showed mutations in CALR and MPL.

Myeloproliferative neoplasm NOS in a patient with mild anaemia, splenomegaly, and splanchnic venous thrombosis not meeting the clinical, morphological, and molecular diagnostic criteria for any of the specific myeloproliferative neoplasms. Bone marrow trephine biopsy highlights hypercellular-for-age marrow with increased megakaryocytes with occasional tight clusters, and with eosinophilia, panmyelosis (unusual in prefibrotic primary myelofibrosis), and minimal fibrosis (<<35693>>). Higher-magnification view highlighting the atypical megakaryocytes in clusters (<<35694>>). Reticulin stain shows sparse scattered linear reticulin fibres with rare intersections (<<35695>>).

title: Diagnostic criteria for myeloproliferative neoplasm NOS (unclassifiable)
tablehtml:
Requires all three of the following:

·      Presence of features of any one of the following features:

o   Clinical and haematological features of an MPN (e.g. splenomegaly, leukocytosis, thrombocytosis) in the absence of significant monocytosis and significant eosinophilia

o   Bone marrow hypercellularity with megakaryocytic hyperplasia and varying degrees of granulocytic and erythroid hyperplasia, without dysplastic features

o   Clinical and morphological features can be discrepanta

·      Not meeting criteria for any other MPN, MDS, MDS/MPNb, or myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions

·      Presence of driver mutations such as JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutations, or another clonal markerc

Requires the absence of both of the following:

·      Insufficient clinical data or inadequate bone marrow specimen for accurate evaluation and classification

·      Recent history of cytotoxic or growth factor therapy, particularly when dysplastic features are seen

CML, chronic myeloid leukaemia; MDS, myelodysplastic neoplasm; MDS/MPN, myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm; MPN, myeloproliferative neoplasm; NOS, not otherwise specified.

aIn the pathology report, it is important to describe the morphological findings, summarize the reasons for the difficulty in the classification of a specific MPN subtype, specify any particular MPN types that can be excluded, and recommend additional workup such as expanded molecular testing or repeat peripheral blood / bone marrow within a reasonable duration for further classification. bEffects of any previous treatment, severe comorbidity, and changes during the natural progression of the disease process must be excluded. cIn the absence of any of the three major clonal mutations, a search for other mutations associated with myeloid neoplasms (e.g. ASXL1, EZH2, TET2, IDH1, IDH2, SRSF2, and SF3B1 mutations) and translocations such as those involving ABL1 may be of help in confirming the clonal nature of a suspected MPN-NOS.
